sources.title: Sayantani Pal, IGNOU: Harsha and the Rise of Kanauj, 2020
sources.note: Original university chapter indexed, printed pp.119 and 127, sections 8.1 and 8.4.6-8.5. Direct fetch timed out. Original catalogue confirms author/year. Uses political structure and ending, not speculative hospital interpretation. Geometry caveat is from local decoding.

sources.title: IGNOU BHIC-132: The Pushyabhutis and the Rise of Harsha
sources.note: Original university text indexed, printed p.39, section 3.4.2, early career and eastern campaign. Direct fetch timed out. Avoids unsupported exact territorial sweep. Conservatively combined with overlapping later IGNOU chapter as one work family in checks.

sources.title: Prakrit Text Society: Gaudavaho, foreword
sources.note: Original scholarly edition foreword indexed on text repository, page 8. Vakpati at Yasovarman’s court, close association with Bhavabhuti, eighth-century dating and panegyric. Direct fetch failed; no exact military chronology inferred.

sources.title: Chandrani Banerjee Mukherjee: Yasovarman, Encyclopedia of Ancient History: Asia and Africa (2025)
sources.note: Direct original scholarly abstract read: uncertain lineage, revived Kannauj power and literary court, defeat by Lalitaditya. Exact 733 date omitted because dating varies in scholarship.

sources.title: R. C. Sharma: New Copper Plate of Emperor Harsa, Jnana-Pravaha Annual Bulletin 5 (2002)
sources.note: Original institution PDF indexed text, printed p.225, reproduced query site:jnanapravaha.org/download/research/rep02.pdf "New Copper Plate". Direct PDF gives no extractable text and screenshot failed. Uses accession 2002.29 a-b, material/construction and genealogy only. Reported findspot and uncertain year 23(?) not converted into secure dates.

sources.title: Richard Salomon: Indian Epigraphy, 1998, figure 1 and charter authentication
sources.note: Original scholarly book institutional repository indexed, printed p.70 figure1 exact Banskhera signature and translation; p.117 authentication note says engraved signatures likely copied from an archetype. Direct PDF fetch timed out. Original plate language/date separately corroborated at Indoskript544 as research only; no new attribution charged to that reused runtime source.

sources.title: Bana, Harsa-carita, translated by E. B. Cowell and F. W. Thomas (1897), chapter VII
sources.note: Direct historical primary text in scholarly translation, chapterVII near printed pp.256-258, forest traders and households. This is a literary portrayal, not a statistical household survey. All three chapters below combined as one work for budget.

sources.title: Bana, Harsa-carita, Cowell and Thomas (1897), chapter III
sources.note: Direct primary translation read: Bana’s return to relatives, kin gathered for storytelling; students’ recitation near chapter’s evening scene. No claim all children attended these schools.

sources.title: Bana, Harsa-carita, Cowell and Thomas (1897), chapter V
sources.note: Direct primary translation read: physician Sushena, Prabhakaravardhana’s illness, cooling drinks/boiled water and ritual in royal sickroom, printed pp.172-173. Royal literary scene, not modern treatment advice or evidence for public sanitation.

sources.title: Renate Syed: War, Peace and Chess, Asiatische Studien 62.2 (2008), pp.563-573
sources.note: Original scholarly article on ETH library platform indexed, abstract and opening p.563. Direct fetch cache miss. Author’s interpretation of Bana’s pun and 64-square game is explicitly attributed; speculative clay-piece identification not made certain.

sources.title: Manfred A. J. Eder: Early Terracotta-Figures from Kanauj: Chessmen? Chapter II, South Asian Archaeology 2007, pp.69-84
sources.note: Read original published field-survey article as full scholarly proceedings text on mirror, especially pp.72-74 and conclusions. Identified material is candidate gaming equipment, not a secure complete chess set. Canonical work is BAR International Series2133,2010; mirror access is disclosed.

proposedOverrides.name: Kanauj (Kannauj)
proposedOverrides.summary: Harsha’s northern royal center and later Kannauj courts, with changing regimes distinguished from the imported continuous outline.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Only exact indexed kanauj is associated. No indexed harsha, harshavardhana or pushyabhuti IDs found. Existing broad hindu-kingdoms narrative is not the same entity.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Identical north Indian polygons for600-700 and700-800, bbox76.844568E to88.343083E and24.781696N to32.594060N. Public opening warns this cannot mean continuous government or stable boundaries.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Harsha accession606, death around647; later Yasovarman period only approximate. Historical regime change is not forced to align with century map seams.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Literary household and care scenes are attributed to Bana, not generalized as universal practices. Uncertain copperplate reported provenance/date omitted. No claimed excavation of Harsha’s palace or proof of a complete chess set.
